author: Chamberlin, William Henry
title: The Russian Revolution, 1917-1921, Volume Two: 1918-1921, From the Civil War to the Consolidation of Power
notes: The narrative backbone of the 1918-1922 pack and the only full account of the civil war this project has been able to read end to end: the Internet Archive scan of the **London** edition is out of copyright and downloadable, and every page number cited here was read in it. Chamberlin was the Christian Science Monitor's Moscow correspondent from 1922 to 1934 and wrote from the Soviet published record of the 1920s, from White emigre memoirs and from his own travel; the chronological table (pp. 525-534) and the appendix of translated documents (pp. 465-507) are what a reader will use most. Two warnings. It is a **pre-archival** work: it could not know what opened after 1991, and where it gives a number for the terror or for casualties it is repeating a published claim, not counting. And its pagination is not the New York edition's - a page cited from an American copy will not land in the same place here.
